D018-D013_h001.question_both:
It’s been months now, this nagging feeling, maybe six or seven. Driving the taxi used to be my life, but now… I just go through the motions. Nothing really excites me anymore; even my old bowling league feels like a chore. And that accident, the one with the drunk driver… I keep reliving it. One minute I'm driving, then suddenly I'm back there, the screech of tires, the shattered glass. It’s like a film reel playing in my head, over and over.

Sometimes, after one of those flashbacks, my heart just pounds like crazy. I’ll feel shaky for ages, unable to calm down, even after a minor jolt. It makes even simple things, like deciding what to eat for dinner, feel like a monumental task. I just can't seem to make up my mind about anything. I still can’t shake the anger either; that other driver, he ruined everything. He’s the reason all of this happened. The horror of it all, it's still so fresh, like it just happened yesterday. It just doesn’t fade.
D018-D013_h001.question_a: It's been… I don’t know, about eight months now since the accident. Sometimes, when a car suddenly brakes in front of me, or I hear a certain kind of siren, it’s like I’m right back there again, seeing it all unfold. I pull over, gripping the wheel so hard my knuckles are white, my heart racing, feeling like I’m going to crash all over again. It’s hard to make decisions about anything these days, even what to have for dinner, let alone what route to take on a fare. I just don't have the interest in things I used to enjoy, like going to the local pub with my mates. I've been blaming the city council for not putting up better signs, or that other driver for being careless. That feeling of terror, it just… it hasn't left me. It’s strange, I know I’ve been feeling down, just can’t seem to shake this sadness, and all this low mood, it really started after the crash. I just can’t seem to get over what happened.
D018-D013_h001.question_b:
It’s been rough lately, Doc. This whole thing started a good four months ago, not long after that accident I was in. I was just doing my job, you know, driving my cab, and then... everything changed. I can still see it, clear as day, like I’m right back there in the cab, the screeching brakes, the impact... sometimes I actually feel like I’m there again, the smells, the sounds, even though I know I’m not.

Before all this, I used to love going to the mechanic, tinkering with my car, but now? I just can't bring myself to care. My ex-wife, she keeps blaming me for ruining her life even though I tried to make things right. It's like the shock from that day, the sheer terror, it never really goes away. It just keeps replaying in my head. And then there's the other stuff. I can't even pick out what to wear in the mornings without agonizing over it. If someone honks their horn suddenly, my heart races for ages afterwards, I just can't calm down or get back to normal. I know some of this sounds like what people go through after a bad event, but I also just feel so down and unmotivated for everything, even things not related to the accident. My GP suggested seeing someone about depression, and I think he might be right – it’s like a cloud has settled over everything, affecting every part of my life, not just the memories of that day. What do you think?

Every so often, I’ll just be going about my day, maybe raking out an enclosure, and suddenly I’m right back there, at the scene with the injured tiger. It’s like a movie playing in my head, and I can almost feel the fear again, hear the growls. I try to push those thoughts away, occupy myself, but they just… loop.

My wife says I’m not myself. I get it. I can't seem to relax, even at home. I’m always on edge, always scanning, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen again. It's exhausting. I can’t help but think it was my fault, that I should have done something differently to prevent it. I blame myself, you know?

To be honest, I'm just exhausted. I can’t relax anymore, always on edge, always scanning my surroundings even when I'm at home. It’s like my body is ready to run, even when there’s no danger. This whole thing has just taken such a toll. I don't enjoy anything like I used to. My wife says I’ve been constantly down, and she's right, but it all comes back to that day. I used to love my job, loved making people feel strong, but now? I just go through the motions. I know I'm probably depressed too—I sleep too much, have no energy, and feel numb to everything.
